description:
Tailscode is the native Mac window for every coding agent running on your own machines. Claude Code, opencode and Oh My Pi, on any model they can run, including one on your own graphics card: start them, watch six at once, steer them and read what they did, while each repository stays on the machine that owns it. Your chats go point to point over your own Tailscale network, never through a relay, with no sign-in. Free and open source.

ONE COMMAND TO SET UP
For Claude Code, one line on the computer you code on installs the bridge and ends with a pairing link. Paste it, confirm, and Tailscode has your machine; opencode has a one-line installer too. Want to look first? A built-in demo shows the main screens with no server at all.

EVERY AGENT AT A GLANCE
• The Agents window follows up to six running agents across your machines: the step each one is on, the command it is running or the file it is editing, with approve, answer, nudge and stop, and an inspector that peeks at any of them.
• The sidebar puts who needs you first, then what is working, pinned, saved and recent.
• Split the window into panes and put a different machine, project or conversation in each.

ANY MODEL, EVEN YOUR OWN GPU
• Whatever your agent can run, from cloud models to a local model served by Ollama or llama.cpp on your own machine, picked per chat with its reasoning effort.
• Carry a conversation to another model: the next one gets a short brief of the chat and picks up the thread.
• A party of six favourite models and their effort levels, one click or one chord away.

A LIVE, NATIVE TRANSCRIPT
• Streaming text, with thinking and tool runs folded into one readable trace per turn.
• Syntax-highlighted code with copy, and a diff for every Edit or Write the agent makes.
• Approvals, agent questions as answerable cards, and subagents in the same conversation.
• Queue a follow-up while the agent works, edit it before it lands, or stop the turn on the server.
• In Claude Code chats, the repository, read-only on purpose: branch, upstream drift, staged and changed files, and the diff behind each one.

ASK FROM ANYWHERE
• One global hotkey opens the ask box over any app and sends the question to the machine you choose.
• Not only code: ask what is eating the GPU, research a question, tidy a folder.
• Notifications when a turn needs you or finishes.

KEYBOARD FIRST
One shortcut registry, a vim-mode composer, a cheat sheet, a searchable command list, and a type size for each part of the window.

WHERE THE MONEY WENT
• Every conversation priced turn by turn, every month totalled across machines, by model, project and tool. Always an estimate, never a bill.
• Plan limits and quotas per provider and account.

YOURS, END TO END
• Your chats travel point to point over your tailnet, never through a relay. No sign-in, no ads, no tracking, and your code and conversations never reach us.
• Native AppKit, Swift 6, Liquid Glass, real menus, VoiceOver labels.
• Open source under GPL-3.0: the app, the engine and the bridges. Also on iPhone, iPad and Linux.

FREE, WITH AN HONEST PRO
Every screen but the delegate board is in the free app, on one server, for good. Tailscode Pro is a one-time purchase, no subscription: unlimited servers in one list, iPhone and Mac on the same Apple Account, the delegate board, and a supporter heart.

REQUIREMENTS
A computer on your Tailscale network (free for personal use) running opencode, Claude Code through claude-bridge, or Oh My Pi through omp-bridge. Tailscode is independent open-source software, not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic, Tailscale Inc., the opencode project or Oh My Pi.

Privacy policy: https://midgarcorp.cc/tailscode/privacy
Source code: https://github.com/guitaripod/Tailscode
promotionalText: Run Claude Code, opencode and Oh My Pi on your own computers, on any model they can run, even your own GPU, and watch them all from one native window. No sign-in.
whatsNew:
New:
• Agents window. Board, peek and hour in one window. Now lists what needs you with the answer in place, what is working, what runs in the background and what finished in the last hour. The peek inspector shows what a run is doing, its steps and its context fill; the hour draws a lane per session. Show Agents in the menu or the sidebar opens it.
• Carry a conversation to another model. Picking a model on another machine carries the conversation there as a short brief, and Try with another model on an answer branches the chat from that question. A seam line marks where the answering model changed.
• Six models you carry. The model pill opens a popover of six cards, each a model at a level with an optional name you edit in place. Add to party from the chooser fills the next empty slot.
• Meet Megatron. Thoughts, tool calls and the agent's notes become one head per turn: a collapsed line with its counts, and an open stage with the Metal head, numbered steps, hover cards, pinning, replay and a Share poster. A turn stays one line until you open it. Choose Megatron or Lines in Settings.
• Meridian, a world clock. A chip beside the update mark shows the time here; hover for pinned places and quota windows about to reopen, and click for lanes, alarms and copy as ISO, UTC or epoch.
• Talk to the agent, in beta. A call strip above the composer listens and types into the chat on its model and effort, with mute and hang up. It is an ear, not a voice.
• The usage share is modular. Pick a format for X, a square, a portrait or the full column, choose modules, then copy the caption or image, save or share. A month that ran mostly on your own machine leads with that work.
• First run is one checklist: the machine on your tailnet, a pairing link, claude-bridge installed, and the proof it answers.
• A machine proves it can paint and render before you ask; the picture and video studios list every missing ComfyUI model file and node, with a copy-the-command row.
• Quotas are one card per provider and account, with each window's start and reset drawn flat and the reason a machine could not be read.
• The picture gallery is a wide grid, and every tile opens its own picture, with save, share, copy, open and paint again.

Changes:
• The page scrolls past an open Megatron; its step list and account no longer hold the wheel.
• Opening a long chat, and opening or closing Megatron, cost less main-thread time.
• Where the server keeps a queue, queued messages wait there, and edit, cancel and resume go to the server. A paused queue shows a Resume card.
• The App Store build can find your Tailscale machines: Find my machines works there too, with the token kept in the Keychain.
• Game Center sign-in is opt-in, so its banner no longer appears unless you ask for it.

Fixes:
• The quick-ask hotkey no longer crashes the app.
• Crashes on macOS 27.2 are fixed: a click on a capability row and other AppKit callbacks no longer fault.
• Saving a Tailscale token starts the scan, and Save and Cancel answer on the token sheet.
• A Full Disk Access row opens System Settings on the press, even when the server's request fails.
• A turn's pictures and background notes stay inside its Megatron card, and Megatron's account no longer crashes on the turn after an open one.
• The Studio's picture buttons answer the pointer again.
• An open chat takes the model and effort the server has, so a send no longer writes an old level back.
• The chat repaints in the new face when the Mac switches between light and dark.
• Meridian's add-a-place panel answers clicks, and a press inside a sheet no longer closes it.
• The status line holds still when a count or clock changes width.
• A failed quota read keeps the last good numbers, marked as cached.
• opencode 2 conversations get their names, and the chat header shows the title as soon as the server writes it.
